Interactive Explainer Atlas

One concept per page. Each page teaches a single idea through a working simulation you can take apart — every model on this site is checked numerically against closed forms, conservation laws, or published reference values before it ships.

80 explainers · 13 domains · 979 assertions

biology

  • A Mouse Is Not A Small Elephant

    Drag the exponent over fifteen published mammals. Metabolic rate goes as mass to 0.76, not the 2/3 a surface-area argument predicts, and a wrong exponent shows up as a tilt rather than as scatter.

    ●●○○○ compare-side-by-side 13 checks

  • The Null Model Every Population Fails

    Hardy-Weinberg drawn on a de Finetti triangle. Switch selection and mutation on and watch a population leave the curve and be dragged back onto it, and see how slowly a recessive can be removed.

    ●●○○○ perturb-and-observe 13 checks

  • Below This Current, Nothing Happens

    A neuron charges like a leaky capacitor until it trips a threshold, fires, and resets. Drag the input current down and at one exact value the output stops entirely.

    ●●●○○ drag-parameter 13 checks

  • Herd Immunity Is Not Where It Stops

    Guess how many people an unmitigated epidemic infects, then watch it sail past the herd immunity threshold and keep going.

    ●●●○○ guess-then-reveal 12 checks

  • Kill Both Sides, Help the Pest

    Explore the Lotka-Volterra phase plane, find that every orbit averages to the equilibrium it never sits at, and see why culling predator and prey together makes the prey more common.

    ●●●○○ spatial-explore 12 checks

  • One Number Decides Whether a Population Settles

    Raise the growth rate of a one-line population model and watch it settle, split, split again, and then stop repeating altogether.

    ●●●○○ time-scrubber 11 checks

  • Which Number Did the Poison Move?

    Add an inhibitor to an enzyme assay and watch which of the two parameters changes — the one that holds still names the mechanism.

    ●●●○○ perturb-and-observe 12 checks

chemistry

  • Ten Degrees Doubles It, But Only Near Room Temperature

    The Arrhenius law is exponential in one over temperature, not in temperature. Nudge the rail ten kelvin at a time and watch a rule of thumb everyone learns as a constant slide from 2.70 down to 1.29.

    ●●○○○ perturb-and-observe 12 checks

  • A Flat Battery Is Not Empty

    Drag the concentrations in a two-beaker cell and watch its voltage move, then follow the free-energy curve down to the bottom where the voltage is exactly zero.

    ●●●○○ drag-parameter 12 checks

  • It Only Undoes Part of What You Did

    Disturb a gas equilibrium and it shifts to oppose you, but only partly, and of the three obvious disturbances just one moves the equilibrium constant itself.

    ●●●○○ perturb-and-observe 13 checks

  • The Balanced Equation Will Not Tell You This

    Four unlabelled vials of decaying reactant. Tune an order and a rate constant until your law lies on the measurements, and learn to read the order off the shape of the curve.

    ●●●○○ tune-to-match 12 checks

  • The Flat Part of the Curve

    Titrate a weak acid and watch pH refuse to move, then give way all at once, and find the closed form for how much punishment a buffer absorbs.

  • Where The Ideal Gas Law Quietly Stops Working

    On a log-log chart PV = nRT is a straight line. Squeeze a real gas and it peels away: below the line while attraction wins, above it once the molecules run out of room.

    ●●●○○ perturb-and-observe 13 checks

computer science

  • The Slower Algorithm Wins For A While

earth science

economics

  • Raise The Price Until Elasticity Is One

    A price rise earns more on every unit you still sell and loses the units you no longer sell. One number decides which wins, and the revenue peak sits exactly where it is minus one.

    ●●○○○ drag-parameter 13 checks

engineering

  • Depth Beats Width, Cubically

    Tune a beam's section until it meets the span/360 sag limit. Depth is cubed in the answer and width appears once, which is why joists are tall and thin and why a plank laid flat is useless.

    ●●○○○ tune-to-match 13 checks

    Build a gear train one wheel at a time and watch an idler flip the direction without touching the ratio, while two wheels bolted to one shaft change everything.

  • The Delay You Cannot Tune Away

    A delay between acting and seeing is the one thing a controller cannot tune around. Past one gain, set by the delay alone, the loop oscillates whatever you do to it.

    ●●●○○ tune-to-match 12 checks

  • The Far End of the Fin Is Cold

    A longer cooling fin always dissipates more heat and always dissipates less per millimetre of metal. Put two fins side by side and watch the second one waste its length.

    ●●●○○ compare-side-by-side 13 checks

  • Three Knobs, Three Different Ways to Be Wrong
